HISTORY, SUPERSEDED BY THE DESTRUCTOR FOLD (last boundary_evidence entry): EMISSION ORDER -- MEASURED REFUSAL, not a near-miss. The ROM puts D0 (0x02139f70) BELOW D1 (0x02139fc8). daObjFallBlock_c.h defines `~daObjFallBlock_c() {}` in the class body, and an in-class inline destructor emits D1 then D0; the only other admissible spelling, out of line, emits D2/D0/D1. Scaffolds change nothing (the two legacy shards carried one each and both are dropped here). So the licensed run cannot be put in ROM order without spelling the destructor out of line, and the cartridge refuses that spelling: config/arm9/overlays/ov098/relocs.txt carries exactly two inbound references to the pair -- from:0x0213c5fc to:0x02139fc8 and from:0x0213c600 to:0x02139f70 -- which are _ZTV16daObjFallBlock_c + 0x40 and + 0x44 off the address point, i.e. vtable slots 16 and 17, the two the header already names. NO instruction in the image calls either address, and no _ZN16daObjFallBlock_cD2Ev exists in the image or in any symbols.txt -- an out-of-line base destructor would make each of the four descendants call D2 and would leave it live. The in-class inline body is the cartridge's form. Same shape daObjFloatBoard_c settled at (notes/agents/roles/writer.md, 'When a subset is the right answer'), and settled the same way here: the licensed set is cut to the orderable 10 and the destructor pair is held out as deadstrip-duplicate against its own ROM homes. The 12/12 evidence is not discarded -- it is preserved in this branch's first commit and in the partial_isolation block below, which records a 12-object PARTIAL-LINK-VERIFIED run whose ROM is byte-identical to the stock control.

TWO ROWS THE SIBLING ORACLE COULD NOT WRITE, AND WHY. (1) ov098/daObjYajirusi_c.json recorded that _ZN7Vector3D1Ev fits neither policy schema because compiler_only_output refuses a symbol with a configured ROM home. That note is now doubly stale: tubuild.py grew `deadstrip-duplicate` for exactly this case -- a FUNCTION with a ROM home another source owns (arm9 0x020072c0) -- and verify accepts it here (`compiler-only : exact deadstrip ['_ZN7Vector3D1Ev']`). This class's own _ZTI16daObjFallBlock_c and _ZTS16daObjFallBlock_c CAN be canonical-imported because mwld's one kept copy of them is not in this module at all: ov015 owns both (0x02114874 / 0x0211488c) and ov098's vtable header word relocates across to them. The vtable itself is the one record that stays in this module, so it takes deadstrip-data against its own ov098 home at 0x0213c5bc. All ten RTTI records take deadstrip-data too, each against the module that actually owns it -- arm9 for the fBase_c/dBase_c/dActor_c pairs, ov002 for dBgActor_c's, ov015 for this class's own -- verified row by row against those modules' symbols.txt.

WHY THIS PROMOTED FIRST. An earlier revision of this entry concluded promotion was refused, because it had routed the ten _ZTI/_ZTS records to externalized_output and tubuild.py:5861 refuses promotion outright for any entry carrying that block ('promotion does not yet persist externalized_output policy'). That routing was the error, not the verdict: every one of the ten has a configured ROM home, so each is deadstrip-data in compiler_only_output, the entry carries no externalized_output at all, and promotion is admissible. daObjYajirusi_c stayed text-verified for the same routing reason, not because its own-module homes are unlicensable: every one of its records likewise has a configured ROM home outside the claimed .text span, so each takes deadstrip-data the same way (see ov098/daObjYajirusi_c.json, promoted alongside). What remains true of the destructor ordering is that it bounds the promotion to 10 of 12, not that it blocks it.

FORCING FUNCTIONS AND PRAGMA. This TU compiles under `#pragma defer_codegen off` and carries two uncalled functions, daObjFallBlock_c_EmitDeletingDestructor and daObjFallBlock_c_EmitDestructor, recorded as compiler_only_output deadstrip rows. They are the parse-time trigger that places D0 then D1 ahead of the real members and are not in the ROM. The destructor itself stays inline in include/daObjFallBlock_c.h because the class's descendants inline its vptr store.

The class destructor is defined inline in its header because the descendants inline its vptr store, so no file can define it out of line; a delete-expression asks for the deleting variant by name. This file compiles under `#pragma defer_codegen off`, where ordinary functions are emitted at parse time in source order -- the only measured lever that makes mwccarm emit D0 before D1 as the cartridge has them -- and this forcer is the parse-time trigger that places D0 first. Emitted between the licensed D0 and D1 sections. Homeless: config/ has no symbol row for it.

This file compiles under `#pragma defer_codegen off`, where ordinary functions are emitted at parse time in source order, so the call places D1 after D0 as the cartridge has them. Emitted between the licensed D1 section and the first real member, so it does not disturb the licensed run. Homeless: config/ has no symbol row for it.
